advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the unbacked-citation coaching string to mention that an ancestor (parent) edge also grounds the citation, matching the new inherited-edge semantics.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_citation.py:168: `f"citation [rebar:{cited_id}] ({subj!r}) names no VERIFIED upstream prerequisite: "`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_citation.py:169: `f"P neither declares \`depends_on -> {cited_id}\` nor is blocked by it. Add a "`
Docstring at line 158-161 was updated to mention the inherited ancestor path, but the emitted issue string at 167-172 was not — the coaching diverges from the new semantics.
advisory.finding: The unbacked-citation coaching message was not updated for the inherited-edge path: it only advises adding a direct `depends_on` edge on P or ensuring `C blocks P`, never that an ancestor edge grounds the citation. For a child ticket relying on the parent's promoted dependency (the case this feature targets), the advice steers the author toward a direct child->C edge, contradicting the by-design hierarchy promotion.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Memoize/coalesce the per-ticket show_ticket read so the ancestor walk fetches each ticket's parent_id and deps once rather than twice per ancestor.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:506: `return _reads.show_ticket(cid, repo_root=ctx.tickets_root).get("deps", []) or []`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:511: `return _reads.show_ticket(cid, repo_root=ctx.tickets_root).get("parent_id") or None`

det_citation.py:101 and 109 call resolve_parent(current) then resolve_deps(parent) inside the bounded walk (_MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK = 32), so each ancestor triggers two full show_ticket reads for data one read supplies.
orchestrator.py:92-94 note the run-scoped memo is on assemble_context; these p6 resolvers bypass it and read fresh each call.
advisory.finding: The injected `_resolve_parent` and `_resolve_deps` each call `_reads.show_ticket` uncached, and the ancestor walk calls both per ancestor — so a single `show_ticket` (which already returns both `parent_id` and `deps`) is fetched twice per ancestor, up to ~64 store reads per citation for a deep or cyclic chain, multiplied across all citations.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test injecting a raising `resolve_parent` (and a raising `resolve_deps` during the ancestor walk) asserting the citation stays UNBACKED and no exception escapes.
evidence: det_citation.py:100-103 `parent = resolve_parent(current)` ... `except Exception: ... return False`
det_citation.py:108-111 `anc_deps = resolve_deps(parent) or []` ... `except Exception: ... return False`
ABSENCE: no test in test_det_citation_inherited.py passes a resolver that raises; _resolvers (lines 20-21) returns only non-raising lambdas
test_det_citation.py:114 test_reverse_lookup_error_fails_closed covers only the direct path (called without resolve_parent)
advisory.finding: The new inherited-edge ancestor walk documents a FAIL-CLOSED contract on `resolve_parent` raising (det_citation.py:100-103) and on `resolve_deps(parent)` raising mid-walk (det_citation.py:108-111), but no test injects a raising resolver on these paths. The pre-existing fail-closed test (test_det_citation.py:114) exercises only the direct reverse-lookup with no resolve_parent, so both new except-branches are regression-blind: removing them (letting the exception propagate) would fail no test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two tests: one where resolve_parent raises RuntimeError (assert len(issues)==1), and one where resolve_parent succeeds but resolve_deps(parent) raises (assert len(issues)==1).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a multi-hop test where only a grandparent (2+ levels up) carries the depends_on/blocks edge to C and assert the child's citation is grounded.
evidence: det_citation.py:99-117 loop `for _ in range(_MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK): ... current = parent` supports >1 hop
ABSENCE: all inherited tests use parents `{B: A, A: None}` (lines 27, 37, 47) — no grandparent (e.g. `{B: A, A: G, G: None}` with only G carrying the edge)
advisory.finding: The ancestor walk supports multi-level inheritance (loop with `current = parent`, det_citation.py:117) but every test uses a single parent hop with the parent's parent set to None (`{B: A, A: None}`). The grandparent-grounds-the-citation path is untested, so a regression that stops the walk after the first hop would pass all current tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: deps = {G: [{'relation':'depends_on','target_id':C}], C: []}; parents = {B: A, A: G, G: None}; assert unbacked_citations(CITES, [], resolve_deps, B, resolve_parent=resolve_parent) == []

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with an acyclic parent chain longer than _MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK where the grounding edge sits beyond the bound, asserting the citation stays UNBACKED (bound enforced).
evidence: det_citation.py:70 `_MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK = 32`
det_citation.py:104 `if not parent or parent in seen: return False` — the cycle guard the existing test hits
test_det_citation_inherited.py:67 `_resolvers(deps, {B: A, A: B})` is a 2-node cycle caught by `seen`, not by the depth bound
advisory.finding: The `_MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK = 32` depth bound (det_citation.py:70,99) is not exercised. The only bounding test uses a 2-node cycle `{B: A, A: B}` which is caught by the `seen`-set guard (line 104), a different mechanism than the range() depth cap. A long acyclic chain exceeding 32 levels (which the bound exists to terminate) has no test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve P's ancestor chain (and per-ancestor deps) once per `unbacked_citations` invocation instead of re-walking it inside `_inherited_edge_verified` for every citation.
evidence: `unbacked_citations` loops per citation: `for subject, cited_id in citations:` then `if _edge_verified(cited_id, own_deps, resolve_deps, plan_ticket_id, resolve_parent):` (det_citation.py:163-164); `citations` comes from `parse_citations(ctx.plan_text)` (det_floor.py:514) — user-controlled N.

`_inherited_edge_verified` re-derives the parent chain each call: `current = plan_ticket_id` then `for _ in range(_MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK): parent = resolve_parent(current) ... anc_deps = resolve_deps(parent)` (det_citation.py:97-117). The chain P->A->... does not depend on `cited_id`, so it is identical for every citation.

Injected resolvers are unmemoized disk reads: `_resolve_parent`/`_resolve_deps` both call `_reads.show_ticket(cid, repo_root=ctx.tickets_root)` (det_floor.py:505-511); `show_ticket` -> `show_state` does `resolve_ticket_id` + `reduce_ticket` event-log replay per call (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:277-299).
ABSENCE: no caching/memoization on these resolvers on the plan-review path — the only lru_cache in the package is in registry.py:212/318, not applied here.
advisory.finding: The ancestor parent-chain of the plan ticket P is invariant across all citations, but `_inherited_edge_verified` re-walks it from scratch for every unbacked citation, re-issuing identical `resolve_parent`/`resolve_deps` `show_ticket` disk-read+reduce calls with no memoization. For N citations this repeats up to ~32 identical ancestor reads N times.
scenarios: A plan ticket P nested several levels deep (P->A->...->root) whose plan text carries many `[rebar:<id>]` citations that are not directly edge-backed: each unbacked citation re-walks and re-reads the entire ancestor chain from disk.
Deep hierarchies (near the 32-level bound) combined with many citations multiply the redundant reads.
advisory.suggested_fix: Hoist the ancestor walk out of the per-citation path: compute the bounded ancestor id list (and their deps) once in `unbacked_citations`, or wrap `resolve_parent`/`resolve_deps` in a per-call memo (e.g. `functools.lru_cache`/dict cache) so identical ids are read once. Then check each cited_id against the pre-resolved ancestor deps.
